questions.stem: « Il a eu son bac ! » What does it mean?
options: He sat the bac
He failed the bac
He is revising for the bac
He passed the bac
questions.explanation: « Avoir son bac » means to pass it. Sitting it is « passer le bac », a well-known false friend: « passer » an exam does not mean passing it.

questions.stem: What average mark out of 20 does a student need to pass the bac?
questions.explanation: French marks are out of 20, and an overall average of 10 passes. A student between 8 and 10 can sit extra oral exams to try to reach 10.

questions.stem: A bac « mention bien » means an average of at least what?
options: 14 out of 20
12 out of 20
16 out of 20
10 out of 20
questions.explanation: The honours are « assez bien » from 12, « bien » from 14 and « très bien » from 16. An average of 10 passes with no mention.

questions.stem: « Avec 9 de moyenne, elle va au rattrapage. » What does this mean?
options: She has to repeat the whole final year again at her lycée
She has failed, with no chance to improve her result
She has passed and been awarded an honours mention
She will sit extra oral exams to try to reach the pass mark
questions.explanation: « Le rattrapage » (the second group of exams) is for students averaging between 8 and 10: oral exams that can lift the result to a pass. Below 8, the bac is failed.

questions.stem: What is « le grand oral » of the bac?
options: a speech that the top student gives at the graduation ceremony
an oral exam testing the student's level in English
a public debate between lycées broadcast on national radio
an oral exam on a question linked to the student's specialty subjects
questions.explanation: In the grand oral, students present a question they have prepared, linked to their specialty subjects, then discuss it with a jury of two teachers.

questions.stem: What is Parcoursup?
options: a careers fair held in every French lycée at the end of the year
a revision app published by the Ministry of Education
a scholarship for students who pass the bac with honours
the national online platform for applying to higher education
questions.explanation: Final-year students list their choices of university courses and other programs on Parcoursup, and receive offers there.

questions.stem: « Le jour des résultats, les lycéens se pressent devant les panneaux pour chercher leur nom. » What happens?
options: Students crowd around the lists to see if they passed
Students hand in their final exam papers to teachers
Students vote for their class representative
Students queue up to enrol for the next school year
questions.explanation: Results are posted on boards at the lycée as well as online, and checking « les panneaux » is a scene of tears and celebration each July.

questions.stem: What is « un bac blanc »?
options: a bac with no marks
a failed bac result
a practice bac exam
a bac taken in winter
questions.explanation: « Un bac blanc » is a mock exam set by the lycée to prepare students for the real thing.

questions.stem: « Il a été recalé au bac, mais il le repassera l'an prochain. » What happened?
options: He failed the bac and will sit it again
He passed the bac and will now study more
He missed the bac because he was ill
He passed the bac at the second attempt
questions.explanation: « Être recalé » is informal for failing an exam, and « repasser » means to sit it again. The future « repassera » shows the second attempt has not happened yet.

questions.stem: « Après les épreuves, toute la classe est partie fêter ça à la plage. » What are « les épreuves » here?
options: the exams
the rehearsals
the school holidays
the class photos
questions.explanation: « Une épreuve » is an exam or test, as in « les épreuves du bac ». The class celebrated once the exams were over.

questions.stem: « En Australie, on fête la fin du lycée avec un bal et les “schoolies” ; en France, il n'y a pas vraiment de cérémonie, mais on fait la fête entre amis après les résultats. » What contrast is drawn?
options: France holds a formal ball where Australia holds none
Neither country marks the end of school in any way
French students celebrate before the results come out
Australia has more organised end-of-school traditions
questions.explanation: The writer lists a ball and schoolies for Australia, but « pas vraiment de cérémonie » for France, where friends celebrate informally after the results.

questions.stem: In Québec, what is « le bal des finissants »?
options: a formal ball marking the end of secondary school
a farewell party for teachers who are retiring
a dance competition between Québec high schools
a graduation ceremony for university students
questions.explanation: « Les finissants » are students finishing their studies. The ball at the end of secondary school is a major rite of passage in Québec, with formal dress and photos.

questions.stem: What is « la remise des diplômes »?
options: the date when students enrol in courses
the replacement of a diploma that was lost
the ceremony where diplomas are handed out
the marking of the final exam papers
questions.explanation: « Remettre » means to hand over, so « la remise des diplômes » is a graduation ceremony.

questions.stem: « Ça y est, on est diplômés ! On va enfin pouvoir tourner la page. » What does « tourner la page » mean here?
options: to begin reading a brand-new book
to forget everything learnt at school
to go back and repeat the final year
to move on to a new chapter of life
questions.explanation: « Tourner la page » is to put a stage of life behind you and move on. « Ça y est » means 'that's it, we've done it'.

questions.stem: « Le lycée, je ne le regretterai pas… mais mes copains, eux, vont me manquer. » How does the speaker feel?
options: indifferent to both school and friends
keen to repeat the final year with friends
glad to leave school but sad to leave friends
sad to leave school but glad to leave friends
questions.explanation: « Je ne le regretterai pas » means she won't miss school, while « mes copains vont me manquer » means she will miss her friends. Remember that with « manquer » the thing missed is the subject.

questions.stem: « La remise des diplômes marque un rite de passage : on quitte l'adolescence pour entrer dans la vie d'adulte. » What is claimed about the ceremony?
options: It celebrates passing a driving test at eighteen
It is mainly a chance for families to take photos
It marks the move from adolescence into adult life
It is a tradition now losing its meaning for teenagers
questions.explanation: « Un rite de passage » marks a transition between stages of life. Here, graduation symbolises leaving adolescence behind.

questions.stem: In France, what is the difference between « le bénévolat » and « le volontariat », such as the service civique?
options: Bénévolat is unpaid help in free time; volontariat is a set commitment with an allowance
Bénévolat is a paid job in a charity; volontariat is unpaid help given in free time
Bénévolat is only for retired people; volontariat is only for school students
There is no difference: both are unpaid help given whenever you have time
questions.explanation: A « bénévole » gives time freely without pay. A « volontaire » signs up for a defined mission, often full-time for months, and receives a monthly allowance, not a salary.

questions.stem: Who can do a « service civique » in France?
options: young people aged 16 to 25, or up to 30 with a disability
only university graduates who already hold a degree
retired people over 60 who want to stay active
children under 16 during the school holidays
questions.explanation: The service civique is open to 16- to 25-year-olds, and to 30 for young people with a disability, with no diploma required.

questions.stem: How long does a service civique mission last?
options: 3 to 4 years
one day a month
6 to 12 months
1 to 2 weeks
questions.explanation: A service civique is a mission of 6 to 12 months, for at least 24 hours a week, serving the community in areas such as health, education, the environment or sport.

questions.stem: A service civique advertisement describes « une mission d'intérêt général ». What is that?
options: a task that serves the whole community
a secret task with a special agency
a general knowledge quiz for volunteers
a well-paid job with a large company
questions.explanation: « L'intérêt général » is the common good, so the mission benefits the public rather than a business.

questions.stem: What is « une maraude »?
options: a charity concert held to raise money for a good cause
a sponsored run organised by a sports club
a clean-up of rubbish on a beach or in a park
a round to bring food and support to homeless people
questions.explanation: Volunteers on « une maraude » walk or drive through a city, often at night, offering food, warm drinks and a chat to people sleeping rough.

questions.stem: What is « une collecte alimentaire »?
options: a food drive
a picnic
a cooking class
a food delivery app
questions.explanation: « Une collecte » is a collection, so « une collecte alimentaire » gathers donated food for people in need, often outside supermarkets.

questions.stem: « Je donne un coup de main à la banque alimentaire le samedi. » What does the speaker do on Saturdays?
options: buys food for the family
helps out at the food bank
donates money to a local bank
works as a bank teller
questions.explanation: « Donner un coup de main » is an idiom for lending a hand. « La banque alimentaire » is a food bank, not a financial bank.

questions.stem: « Elle s'est engagée dans une association de défense de l'environnement. » What does « s'engager » mean here?
options: to get engaged to be married
to be hired for a paid job
to sign up to the army
to get involved and commit
questions.explanation: « S'engager dans une association » is to commit your time to a cause. « Se fiancer » means to get engaged to be married.

questions.stem: Who are « les bénéficiaires » of a charity?
options: the people who donate
the paid staff
the board members
the people it helps
questions.explanation: « Les bénéficiaires » benefit from the charity's help. Donors are « les donateurs ».

questions.stem: « Le bénévolat m'a donné confiance en moi et m'a permis d'acquérir des compétences que je peux mettre sur mon CV. » Which benefits does the speaker name?
options: university credit and a scholarship
free travel and accommodation abroad
confidence and skills to list on a CV
a salary and a permanent job offer
questions.explanation: « Confiance en moi » is self-confidence and « des compétences » are skills. Nothing is said about pay, study credit or travel.

questions.stem: « On voudrait tous aider, mais entre les études, le petit boulot et la famille, où trouver le temps ? » What challenge is raised?
options: a lack of interest among young people
finding the time to volunteer
finding a charity that needs help
the cost of joining an association
questions.explanation: The rhetorical question « où trouver le temps ? » points to time pressure from study, a casual job and family. « On voudrait tous aider » rules out a lack of interest.

questions.stem: « Sans les bénévoles, beaucoup de clubs sportifs devraient fermer leurs portes. » What is claimed?
options: Sports clubs pay their volunteers a good wage
Most sports clubs no longer accept volunteers
Many sports clubs depend on volunteers to survive
Volunteers are forcing many sports clubs to close
questions.explanation: « Sans » plus the conditional « devraient fermer » says what would happen without volunteers: clubs would close. It shows the benefit to communities.

questions.stem: « En Australie, des milliers de pompiers bénévoles luttent contre les feux de brousse. » What does this show?
options: Bushfires in Australia are fought only by the army
Australian firefighters are all highly paid professionals
Volunteers are not allowed to fight bushfires
Volunteer firefighters play a major role against bushfires
questions.explanation: Rural fire services in Australia rely heavily on volunteers, a strong example of how volunteering serves communities.

questions.stem: After helping at a shelter, a volunteer says « Ça m'a fait chaud au cœur ». What does she mean?
options: It warmed my heart
It made me feel ill
It made me angry
It wore me out
questions.explanation: « Faire chaud au cœur » means to touch or warm the heart. It describes the emotional reward of helping others.

questions.stem: « Certains reprochent aux jeunes de faire du bénévolat seulement pour enrichir leur CV. Et alors ? Si la cause en profite, où est le problème ? » What is the writer's position?
options: The motive matters less than the help given
Volunteering to boost a CV is dishonest
Young people should stop volunteering
Volunteers ought to be paid for their work
questions.explanation: The writer reports a criticism, then dismisses it with « Et alors ? » and a rhetorical question: if the cause benefits, the motive is not a problem.

questions.stem: « Au début, j'y allais à reculons ; aujourd'hui, je ne raterais une maraude pour rien au monde. » How has the volunteer's attitude changed?
options: from reluctance to real commitment
from enthusiasm to growing boredom
from commitment to wanting to quit
from fear of the dark to confidence
questions.explanation: « Y aller à reculons » means to go reluctantly, and « pour rien au monde » means not for anything. The conditional « je ne raterais » shows how much it now matters to her.

questions.stem: « Faire du bénévolat à l'étranger, c'est bien ; mais certains projets coûtent cher et aident surtout… les organisateurs. » What is the writer's attitude?
options: enthusiastic about every overseas volunteering trip
angry that volunteers are not allowed to travel
neutral, giving only facts about the projects
sceptical about some overseas volunteering projects
questions.explanation: « C'est bien ; mais » concedes a point before a criticism, and the pause before « les organisateurs » adds irony: the projects mainly benefit those who run them.
